name: Goldshire
summary: Goldshire stands where Elwynn’s roads meet, between Stormwind City, Westfall, Redridge, and the southern frontier. Rebuilt after the First War, it offers travelers the Lion’s Pride Inn, while a hard-pressed Stormwind Guard defends the town.

sections.title: A Crossroads Under Strain
sections.body: Goldshire holds the crossroads in rural Elwynn, where the king’s highways meet. Threats press closer as Stormwind’s forces thin and King Varian Wrynn remains mysteriously absent. Marshal Dughan must rely on passing adventurers instead of regular troops to guard the borders. Riverpaw gnolls push in from the west, while hostile murlocs claim the shores of Stone Cairn Lake and Crystal Lake. Their attacks have killed royal guards and brought danger close to town.

sections.title: Scars of the Great Wars
sections.body: Goldshire and Moonbrook were the last strongholds to fall in the First War. Warchief Blackhand cut King Llane Wrynn I off from his realm before sacking Stormwind Keep, and the Orcish Horde overwhelmed both towns. Goldshire was reduced to ash and lay barren until it was rebuilt after the Second War.

faq.q: Who is in charge of defending Goldshire?
faq.answer: Marshal Dughan of the Stormwind Guard commands Goldshire’s defenses. He coordinates the garrison from the town center, but a lack of reinforcements leaves him hiring freelance adventurers to face border threats and monster bounties.

faq.q: What threats are currently menacing the town?
faq.answer: Riverpaw gnolls raid east toward Westbrook Garrison, while hostile murlocs infest Stone Cairn Lake and Crystal Lake. Local scouts warn that the skirmishes could reach Goldshire’s streets without intervention.

faq.q: What happened to Goldshire during the First War?
faq.answer: Goldshire was one of the last two human towns to fall before Stormwind was sacked. Warchief Blackhand destroyed it alongside Moonbrook to sever King Llane’s supply lines, leaving it in ruins until its rebuilding after the Second War.

faq.q: Why is the Lion's Pride Inn so notable?
faq.answer: The Lion’s Pride Inn is one of Azeroth’s most respected and frequented alehouses. At the junction of several regional highways, it is a meeting hall, resting place, and training ground for travelers crossing the kingdom.

angles.text: As a human fresh from Northshire Abbey, you find Goldshire offers your first real taste of the kingdom beyond the monastery walls and a sobering view of Stormwind’s strained borders.
As an Alliance traveler, you pass through Goldshire on the way from the capital to the frontier lands of Westfall, Redridge, and Duskwood.
